newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila call loan rates up, govt funds quit PNB.
newsitem.headline: Manila call loan rates up, govt funds quit PNB.

text.p: Philippine overnight money edged higher to an average of 12.59375 percent on Wednesday from 12.40625 as tight liquidty persisted, dealers said.
Banks have tied up their money in reverse repos.

Dealers also believe the system has been drained of liquidity because government funds are being pulled out of Philippine National Bank (PNB). "PNB was the biggest borrower," a dealer at a foreign bank said.
Done rates ranged from 13.25 percent to 11.75 percent. Turnover increased to 24.378 billion pesos from 20.868 billion pesos. Of the 61 participating institutions, 39 were lenders.
One dealer said rates would ease on Thursday after the market ended at its low of 11.75 percent.

Dealers also said T-bill rates have started to fall as the bills mature on a Wednesday. The three-month was quoted at 11.5 percent from the previous day's 11.6; the six-month bills were at 11.9 from 12.0, and the one-year bills were at 12.75 from 12.9.
